sources.title: Electromagnetic Fields Radiated From Electrostatic Discharges: Theory and Experiment
sources.claimBound: Binds electrostatic charge buildup, rapid discharge through air, human-body discharge models and radiated-field interference with electronics.

sources.title: Static Electricity
sources.claimBound: Binds established static-electricity mechanisms and control considerations; it does not identify the mechanism of the reported event.

sources.title: NASA EEE Parts Assurance: Electrostatic Discharge Control Compendium
sources.claimBound: Binds human-generated electrostatic discharge as an engineering risk for sensitive electronic parts used in aerospace work and binds humidity-dependent human charging examples.

sources.title: Controlling Electrical Hazards
sources.claimBound: Binds static electricity and discharge as recognized electrical-hazard concepts within the publication scope.

sources.title: Lightning Facts: St. Elmo's Fire
sources.claimBound: Binds St. Elmo's fire to atmospheric electric fields and pointed or exposed objects; ordinary indoor context is not established by this source.

sources.title: The Precursory Analysis of the Influence of Garments on Corona Discharge Created Around a Human Fingertip
sources.claimBound: Binds photographed fingertip corona in a controlled high-voltage apparatus; it does not show spontaneous ordinary-room fingertip light.

sources.title: The photographs I take with my Xperia have circular lights or appear whitish (Flare, Ghost)
sources.claimBound: Binds lens flare and ghosting as camera-image explanations that can vary with light source and shooting angle.

sources.title: How Are Webb's Full-Color Images Made?
sources.claimBound: Binds detector artifacts, cosmic-ray effects and image processing as separate parts of interpreting bright points in digital imagery.

sources.title: Imaging of Ultraweak Spontaneous Photon Emission from Human Body Displaying Diurnal Rhythm
sources.claimBound: Binds instrument-measured ultraweak human photon emission at intensity far below unaided-eye sensitivity; it does not explain a naked-eye-visible spark.
